premises.text: Busy individuals need help managing household chores.
premises.evidence_span: Dan needs help. Dan needs the butler you never had for the very first time, the luxury of personal service for the rest of us.

premises.text: Alfred provides a service that coordinates multiple household tasks.
premises.evidence_span: Alfred is actually a service lair. It sits on top of other on-demand and local services.

premises.text: Alfred automates the management of household services.
premises.evidence_span: the magic of Alfred is you don't have to make requests. You set things to be automatic.

premises.text: Alfred can customize services based on user preferences.
premises.evidence_span: you can set specific preferences. So, for example, in dry cleaning, Dan likes his clothes folded and maybe light starch.

premises.text: Alfred's model allows for economies of scale by grouping chores.
premises.evidence_span: they group chores, which gives us economies of scale that we can pass along to you.

premises.text: Alfred can scale quickly by partnering with buildings.
premises.evidence_span: we partner with buildings, which allows us to turn on neighborhoods overnight, making us scalable.

premises.text: There is a large market for home services in urban areas.
premises.evidence_span: in Boston alone, there are over 200,000 households who are in our market.

premises.text: The on-demand home services market is growing globally.
premises.evidence_span: on-demand is going global, and anywhere on-demand goes, we come along automatically.

value.text: Individuals can enjoy seamless management of their household chores.
value.evidence_span: Alfred brings together all the services you use seamlessly.

notes: Retention rate and market size are included as evidence of demand but do not constitute separate premises.
